explanation: I searched all of Mathlib, Batteries and Lean core for `FactorsThrough` (case-insensitive, including `factors_through`, `factorsThrough`) and read the API in Mathlib/Logic/Function/Basic.lean (lines 836–972): Mathlib only has `Function.FactorsThrough` with `rfl`, `comp_left`, `comp_right`, `extend*`, `factorsThrough_iff`, `Injective.factorsThrough`, plus unrelated uses (DependsOn, ContinuousMap lift, measure theory, DirichletCharacter's own `FactorsThrough`, homotopy localization). There is no lemma stating that factoring through one base map transports along a commutative square of (locally) ringed spaces, and indeed no transitivity lemma for `FactorsThrough` at all. The closest candidates, `Function.FactorsThrough.comp_right` (giving `FactorsThrough (h.base ∘ u.base) (c.base ∘ u.base)`) and `FactorsThrough.comp_left` (giving `FactorsThrough (v.base ∘ c'.base) c'.base`), each capture only half of the statement; finishing the proof additionally requires rewriting `c.base ∘ u.base` to `v.base ∘ c'.base` via `congrArg Hom.base sq.w` and combining the two results with a hand-written transitivity step, so the result is neither a restatement nor a one- or two-line instantiation of a single Mathlib declaration. The library's own proof unfolds `comp_base`/`comp_apply` and uses `sq.w` directly, applying no Mathlib result.
